summary.text: 家 is written with 宀 above 豕. Early uses are reported for dwelling and household or family. The lower element has competing analyses: a pig beneath a roof, or an abbreviated 豭 used as a sound element. The sound comparison makes the latter plausible if 豭 is the relevant element, but does not establish the earliest sign’s identity. Today 家 commonly means house, home, or family.

formation.text: The construction is disputed. In the traditional phonosemantic analysis, 宀 contributes the dwelling idea and the lower form represents an abbreviated 豭 used for sound. Other analyses treat the lower form as a pig beneath a roof and propose “pig enclosure” as an original meaning. 家 and 豭 match in Mandarin and in the Baxter–Sagart Middle and Old Chinese reconstructions, making a sound role plausible if 豭 is the relevant element. Neither those comparisons nor the pig-enclosure proposal establishes the earliest lower sign’s identity or original meaning.

components.text: 宀 is the roof or dwelling element in the proposed construction. It appears here as a full component; no distinct earlier form is proposed.

The lower element is written 豕 in regular script. The traditional analysis treats it as an abbreviated 豭 used for sound; other analyses see a pig contributing to a scene beneath a roof. Its earliest identity remains disputed.

sound_limitation.text: Matching readings support sound compatibility if 豭 is the relevant element, but do not identify the earliest lower sign or provide a reading for the proposed sign 𢑓.

history.text: The traditional written analysis treats the lower form as an abbreviation of 豭 serving as a sound element; regular script writes 豕 below 宀. This analysis does not establish that 豕 developed graphically from 豭.
One account proposes that an earlier lower sign was 𢑓 and was later altered or misread as 豕. This proposed graphic history remains unverified, and no reading for 𢑓 is established here.

uncertainties.text: The lower element’s earliest identity and role are disputed: it has been interpreted as a pig contributing to the scene or as an abbreviated sound element. The proposed original meaning “pig enclosure” is not established.
Matching readings for 家 and 豭 do not prove that the earliest lower sign was named 豭. No independent ancient pronunciation for the proposed depicted animal or sign is established.

senses.gloss: ancestral temple, family, royal house or household unit
senses.period: Oracle-bone and bronze uses are reported; sequence unresolved
senses.text: Reported uses include ancestral temple and family, royal house or court, and households counted as 家. Their sequence and relationships are unclear.
家 commonly means house or home, and also family. How these current senses connect to the reported early institutional uses is unclear.

developments.text: Both dwelling and household or institutional uses are reported early, but their sequence and any development from one to the other are unresolved.
The modern senses are established, but their chronology and transition from the early reported uses remain unclear.

limitations.text: The reported early uses do not provide a dated sequence of examined inscriptions, so the chronology of these senses remains unresolved.

The pig-enclosure proposal connects a proposed early meaning to human dwelling. The traditional phonetic analysis offers a different account; neither supplies a complete history of the word’s meanings.
